claim: Auxin carries high-definition graded information not only in space but also in time during organogenesis.
source: We used quantitative imaging to demonstrate that auxin carries high-definition graded information not only in space but also in time.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative imaging data presented throughout the manuscript showing spatio-temporal auxin distribution patterns.

claim: During organogenesis, temporal patterns of auxin arise from rhythmic centrifugal waves of high auxin travelling through the tissue faster than growth.
source: We show that, during organogenesis, temporal patterns of auxin arise from rhythmic centrifugal waves of high auxin travelling through the tissue faster than growth.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data and quantitative analysis of auxin maximum movement relative to cell growth.

claim: Temporal integration of auxin concentration is required to trigger the auxin-dependent transcription associated with organogenesis.
source: We further demonstrate that temporal integration of auxin concentration is required to trigger the auxin-dependent transcription associated with organogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by auxin treatment experiments showing time-dependent activation of DR5 reporter and genetic analysis of ett mutants.

claim: Temporal integration of auxin information provides a mechanism to temporally differentiate sites of organ initiation.
source: This provides a mechanism to temporally differentiate sites of organ initiation and exemplifies how spatio-temporal positional information can be used to create rhythmicity.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the experimental data showing delayed transcriptional response and time-dependent auxin signal integration.

claim: Graded distribution of auxin is essential for embryogenesis and post-embryonic development in plants.
source: In plants, graded distribution of the hormone auxin is not only essential for embryogenesis, but also for post-embryonic development, where it regulates the reiterative organogenesis characteristic of plants (Dubrovsky et al., 2008; Vanneste and Friml, 2009; Benková et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Plant shoots develop post-embryonically through rhythmic organ generation in the shoot apical meristem (SAM).
source: Plant shoots develop post-embryonically through rhythmic organ generation in the shoot apical meristem (SAM), a specialized tissue with a stem cell niche in its central zone (CZ; Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about plant development.

claim: In Arabidopsis thaliana, organs are initiated sequentially in the SAM peripheral zone at consecutive relative angles of close to 137°.
source: In Arabidopsis thaliana, as in a majority of plants, organs are initiated sequentially in the SAM peripheral zone (PZ surrounding the CZ) at consecutive relative angles of close to 137°, either in a clockwise or anti-clockwise spiral (Figure 1A; Galvan-Ampudia et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous research and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: DII-VENUS fluorescence reports auxin concentration with cellular resolution in the SAM.
source: In the SAM, DII-VENUS fluorescence reports auxin concentration with cellular resolution (Vernoux et al., 2011; Brunoud et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research establishing DII-VENUS as an auxin biosensor.

claim: qDII produces DII-VENUS and a non-degradable TagBFP reference stoichiometrically from a single RPS5A promoter.
source: qDII differs from previously used tools (Liao et al., 2015) in producing DII-VENUS and a non-degradable TagBFP reference stoichiometrically from a single RPS5A promoter (Wend et al., 2013; Goedhart et al., 2011; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and reference to supplementary figure showing the construct design and expression.

claim: All analyzed meristems showed qDII patterns similar to those obtained with DII-VENUS, with locations of auxin maxima following the phyllotactic pattern.
source: All analyzed meristems (21 individual SAM) showed qDII patterns similar to those obtained with DII-VENUS, with locations of auxin maxima following the phyllotactic pattern (Vernoux et al., 2011; Figure 1B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from 21 individual SAMs and reference to figures showing the patterns.

claim: Auxin distribution follows the same synchronous pattern across a population of SAMs, with low angular and rhythmic variability.
source: Our analysis shows that auxin distribution follows the same synchronous pattern across a population of SAMs, with low angular and rhythmic variability (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D–E, Appendix 2), with apparent stationarity up to a 137° rotation (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of multiple SAMs shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The plastochron lasts 12h ± 2h.
source: This was supported by dissimilarity measurements obtained using different rotation angles between maps (Figure 1—figure supplement 2H), allowing us to confirm that plastochron last 12h ± 2h.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of time-lapse data and rotation angle measurements.

claim: Auxin maxima first appear as finger-like protrusions from a permanent high auxin zone at the center of the SAM.
source: The resulting quantitative temporal map of auxin distribution in the SAM reveals the dynamic genesis of auxin maxima in the PZ first as finger-like protrusions (visible at P-2, P-1 and P0) from a permanent high auxin zone at the center of the SAM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2I–L and Video 1), as previously predicted (de Reuille et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by temporal mapping data shown in supplementary figures and video, and is consistent with previous predictions.

claim: Cells within the auxin maximum zone closest to the CZ at time 0 hr gradually transfer to the depletion zone at time 10 hr.
source: By following a P1 maximum, we observed that cells within the auxin maximum zone closest to the CZ at time 0 hr gradually transfer to the depletion zone at time 10 hr (Figure 2A–C; nuclei circled in white).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing tracked nuclei in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Cells on the distal edge of the maximum zone show a progressive increase in their auxin level over time.
source: At the same time, cells on the distal edge of the maximum zone show a progressive increase in their auxin level (Figure 2A–C; nuclei circled in red), suggesting a spatial shift of the auxin maximum relatively to the cellular canvas.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing tracked nuclei in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The average radial speed of auxin maxima between stages P1 and P4 can surpass the average displacement of individual nuclei, with a peak velocity of more than 1 µm/h at the P2 stage.
source: To explore further this phenomenon, we used nuclear motion to estimate cell motion vectors and compare them with the motion of the center of auxin maximum zones, we further found that the average radial speed of auxin maxima between stages P1 and P4 can surpass the average displacement of individual nuclei, with a peak velocity of more than 1 µm/h at the P2 stage (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of nuclear and auxin maximum motion shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: Auxin maxima are not attached to specific cells; instead they travel through the tissue.
source: These results show that auxin maxima are not attached to specific cells; instead they travel through the tissue, resulting in an apparent centrifugal wave of auxin accumulation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that auxin maxima move faster than cells.

claim: PIN1 concentration increases from P0 and reaches a maximum at P2 before decreasing.
source: Co-visualization of a functional PIN1-GFP (Benková et al., 2003) and qDII/CLV3 fluorescence over time showed that PIN1 concentration increases from P0 and reaches a maximum at P2 before decreasing (Figure 3A,H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), consistent with previous observations (Heisler et al., 2005; Bhatia et al., 2016; Caggiano et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative imaging data shown in Figure 3A,H and supplementary figures, and is consistent with previous research.

claim: At the tissue scale, PIN1 polarity vector maps demonstrate a strong convergence of PIN1 toward the center of the SAM.
source: At the tissue scale, the vector maps demonstrate a strong convergence of PIN1 toward the center of the SAM (Figure 3I–J and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by PIN1 polarity vector maps shown in Figure 3I-J and supplementary figures.

claim: PIN1 polarities deviate locally toward the radial axes followed by auxin maxima when they protrude from the CZ.
source: In addition, PIN1 polarities deviate locally toward the radial axes followed by auxin maxima when they protrude from the CZ.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of PIN1 polarity vector maps in relation to auxin distribution.

claim: Inversion of PIN1 polarities at organ boundaries occurs only from P7, thus isolating the flower from the rest of the SAM from this late stage.
source: We detected the previously observed inversion of PIN1 polarities at organ boundaries (Heisler et al., 2005) and our quantifications show that this occurs only from P7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), thus isolating the flower from the rest of the SAM from this late stage.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in supplementary figures and is consistent with previous observations.

claim: Over the course of one plastochron, only limited changes in the PIN1 polarities are observed.
source: Over the course of one plastochron, only limited changes in the PIN1 polarities are observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that changes in auxin distribution at this time resolution do not require major adjustments in the direction of auxin efflux at the tissue scale.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse analysis of PIN1 polarities shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Only YUC1, YUC4, and YUC6 are expressed in the SAM among the eleven YUC encoding genes.
source: We thus mapped expression of the eleven YUC encoding genes in the SAM, using GFP reporter lines with a promoter fragment size shown to be functional for YUC1,2 and 6 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–N; Liu et al., 2016; Robert et al., 2013). Only YUC1,4,6 were expressed (Figure 3K, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by expression analysis using GFP reporter lines shown in Figure 3K and supplementary figures.

claim: YUC4 is expressed in the L1 layer on the lateral sides of the SAM/flower boundary from P3.
source: While YUC6 showed a very weak expression in the CZ, both YUC1 and YUC4 are expressed in the L1 layer on the lateral sides of the SAM/flower boundary from P3 for YUC4 (Figure 3K) and P4 for YUC1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and D; Cheng et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by expression analysis shown in Figure 3K and supplementary figures.

claim: YUC1 is expressed in the L1 layer on the lateral sides of the SAM/flower boundary from P4.
source: While YUC6 showed a very weak expression in the CZ, both YUC1 and YUC4 are expressed in the L1 layer on the lateral sides of the SAM/flower boundary from P3 for YUC4 (Figure 3K) and P4 for YUC1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and D; Cheng et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by expression analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: From P4, YUC4 expression extends over the entire epidermis of flower primordia.
source: From P4, YUC4 expression extends over the entire epidermis of flower primordia.
evidence: The claim is supported by expression analysis of YUC4 reporter lines.

claim: yuc1yuc4 loss-of-function mutants show severe defects in SAM organ positioning and size.
source: In addition, yuc1yuc4 loss-of-function mutants show severe defects in SAM organ positioning and size (Shi et al., 2018; Pinon et al., 2013; Figure 3L and Figure 3—figure supplement 3O–U).
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic analysis shown in Figure 3L and supplementary figures, and is consistent with previous research.

claim: P3-P5 are auxin production centers for the SAM that regulate phyllotaxis.
source: Taken with the organization of PIN1 polarities, these results suggest that P3-P5 are auxin production centers for the SAM that regulate phyllotaxis and that PIN1 polarity organization allows for pumping auxin away from these production centers and towards the meristem.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combination of YUC expression patterns and PIN1 polarity organization.

claim: Cells expressing DR5 closest to the CZ were robustly positioned at an average distance of 32 µM ± 7 (SD) from the center.
source: Cells expressing DR5 closest to the CZ were robustly positioned at an average distance of 32 µM ± 7 (SD) from the center.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements of DR5 expression position.

claim: The distance from the center at which transcription can be activated by auxin is defined with a near-cellular precision.
source: The distance from the center at which transcription can be activated by auxin is thus defined with a near-cellular precision.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the low standard deviation in DR5 expression position.

claim: Principal Component Analysis shows orthogonality between auxin and DR5 at the tissue scale, indicating absence of a general correlation in the SAM.
source: With the first two axes accounting for around 75% of the observed variability, we unexpectedly observed orthogonality between auxin input and DR5 output, clearly marking the absence of a general correlation in the SAM (Figure 4E, inset).
evidence: The claim is supported by Principal Component Analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Spatially, a given auxin value does not in general determine a specific DR5 value.
source: This demonstrated that, spatially, a given auxin value does not in general determine a specific DR5 value.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of auxin-DR5 relationships shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Values corresponding to primordia at consecutive stages follow loop-like counter-clockwise trajectories in the auxin x DR5 space, symptomatic of hysteresis.
source: However, values corresponding to primordia at consecutive stages follow loop-like counter-clockwise trajectories in the auxin x DR5 space (indicated by the arrow in Figure 4F). Such trajectories are symptomatic of hysteresis reflecting the dependence of a system on its history.
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis shown in Figure 4F demonstrating hysteresis-like behavior.

claim: The start of auxin-induced transcription follows the build-up of auxin concentration with a delay of nearly one plastochron.
source: This showed that the start of auxin-induced transcription follows the build-up of auxin concentration with a delay of nearly one plastochron (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by temporal analysis of auxin and DR5 dynamics shown in Figure 4G-H.

claim: All auxin treatments, even the shorter ones, equally degraded DII-VENUS throughout the PZ.
source: All treatments, even the shorter ones, equally degraded DII-VENUS throughout the PZ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: In shorter auxin treatments (30' and 120'), the auxin transcriptional response was mainly enhanced at P-1 and P-2 and to a lesser extent at the position of the predicted P-3.
source: In the shorter auxin treatments (30' and 120'), the auxin transcriptional response was mainly enhanced at P-1 and P-2 and to a lesser extent at the position of the predicted P-3that is where cells are already being exposed to auxin (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of DR5 expression after auxin treatments shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Longer auxin treatments (300') lead to an activation of signaling in most cells in the PZ and organs.
source: The longer auxin treatments (300') lead to an activation of signaling in most cells in the PZ and organs, with the strongest activation being observed again at P-1 and P-2 but also at the predicted azimuth for P-3, P-4 and P-5 (Figure 5H–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of DR5 expression after auxin treatments shown in Figure 5H-I.

claim: A 300' treatment with 200 nM auxin activated signaling similarly (at P-1) or more strongly (at P-2, P-3, P-4 and P-5) than a 120' 1 mM auxin treatment.
source: We could further show that a 300' treatment with a lower auxin concentration (200 nM) activated signaling similarly (at P-1) or more strongly (at P-2, P-3, P-4 and P-5) than a 120' 1 mM auxin treatment.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of DR5 activation under different auxin treatment conditions.

claim: A 120' treatment with 5 mM auxin lead to an activation of signaling almost as strongly as a 300' 1 mM treatment at P-1, although the activation was lower at P-2.
source: Conversely, a 120' treatment with higher auxin concentration (5 mM) lead to an activation of signaling almost as strongly as a 300' 1 mM treatment at P-1, although the activation was lower at P-2 (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of DR5 activation under different auxin treatment conditions shown in Figure 5I.

claim: DR5 expression was low and radially uniform in pid mutant SAMs, suggesting a uniform auxin distribution.
source: DR5 expression was low and radially uniform in pid SAMs, suggesting a uniform auxin distribution (Figure 5J; Friml et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging of DR5 expression in pid mutants shown in Figure 5J.

claim: In pid mutants treated with 1 mM auxin, DR5 could be activated in all cells of the periphery of the SAM only with a 300' treatment, while a 120' treatment had only a weak effect.
source: When treated with 1 mM auxin, DR5 could be activated in all cells of the periphery of the SAM (suggesting an uptake throughout the PZ as in the wild-type) only with a 300' treatment, while a 120' treatment had only a weak effect (Figure 5J–M and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by auxin treatment experiments on pid mutants shown in Figure 5J-M and supplementary figures.

claim: Even with the reduced complexity in PZ patterning of the pid mutant, activation of auxin signaling is still dependent on the time of exposure to auxin in all cells surrounding the CZ.
source: This indicates that, even with the reduced complexity in PZ patterning of the pid mutant (Friml et al., 2004), activation of auxin signaling is still dependent on the time of exposure to auxin in all cells surrounding the CZ.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that longer auxin treatments are required for DR5 activation in pid mutants.

claim: All cells at the SAM periphery show no intrinsic differences in their capacity to respond to auxin.
source: Notably, the results with pid SAMs suggest that all cells at the SAM periphery show no intrinsic differences in their capacity to respond to auxin, in agreement with published data (Reinhardt et al., 2003a; Heisler et al., 2005; Smith et al., 2006a).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the pid mutant experiments and is consistent with previous research.

claim: In ett-22/arf3 mutants, the expression of DR5 was restricted to only 2–3 cells at sites of organogenesis.
source: We found that in a loss-of function ett3 mutant the expression of DR5 was restricted to only 2–3 cells at sites of organogenesis, an observation consistent with a role for ETT in promoting organogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging of DR5 expression in ett mutants.

claim: In ett mutants, a 300' 1 mM auxin treatment did not induce DR5 in the SAM.
source: In addition, a 300' 1 mM auxin treatment did not induce DR5 in the SAM (Figure 5N–Q and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by auxin treatment experiments on ett mutants shown in Figure 5N-Q and supplementary figures.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of histone deacetylases (HDACs) alone was able to trigger concomitant activation of DR5 at P0 and P-1 sites in the SAM.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of histone deacetylases (HDACs) alone was able to trigger concomitant activation of DR5 at P0 and P-1 sites in the SAM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1Q–S).
evidence: The claim is supported by TSA treatment experiments shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Auxin signal integration likely depends on a functional ARF-dependent auxin nuclear pathway.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that auxin signal integration likely depends on a functional ARF-dependent auxin nuclear pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the ett mutant and HDAC inhibition experiments.

claim: Phyllotaxis is perturbed in ett mutant SAMs.
source: Phyllotaxis is perturbed in ett mutant SAMs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1M–P; Simonini et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging of ett mutant phenotypes shown in supplementary figures and is consistent with previous research.

claim: Daily exogenous auxin treatments at the SAM affected phyllotaxis and the efficiency of the treatment increased with both auxin concentration and treatment length.
source: Supporting this idea, we also found that daily exogenous auxin treatments at the SAM affected phyllotaxis and that the efficiency of the treatment increased with both auxin concentration and treatment length.
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta auxin treatment experiments.

claim: Temporal integration of auxin information at the SAM is essential for phyllotaxis.
source: These results suggest that temporal integration of auxin information at the SAM is essential for phyllotaxis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of auxin treatments and genetic analyses.

claim: Rhythmic organ initiation at the SAM is driven by the combination of high-precision spatio-temporal graded distributions of auxin with the use of the duration of cell exposure to auxin.
source: Our quantitative analysis of the dynamics of auxin distribution and response supports a scenario in which rhythmic organ initiation at the SAM is driven by the combination of high-precision spatio-temporal graded distributions of auxin with the use of the duration of cell exposure to auxin, to temporally differentiate sites of organ initiation (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is a synthesis of the experimental findings presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: A time integration mechanism is essential for rhythmic organ patterning in the SAM since auxin-based spatial information pre-specifies several sites of organ initiation.
source: Importantly our results suggest that a time integration mechanism is essential for rhythmic organ patterning in the SAM since auxin-based spatial information pre-specifies several sites of organ initiation and is thus unlikely to provide sufficient information (Video 1).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that multiple auxin maxima exist simultaneously but organs initiate sequentially.

claim: Temporal integration of the auxin signal likely requires the effectors of the auxin signaling pathway.
source: We provide evidence that temporal integration of the auxin signal likely requires the effectors of the auxin signaling pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments with ett mutants and HDAC inhibitors.

claim: Activation of transcription downstream of auxin by ARFs relies on chromatin remodeling, increasing the accessibility of ARF targets.
source: Activation of transcription downstream of auxin by ARFs relies on chromatin remodeling, increasing the accessibility of ARF targets and possibly allowing for the recruitment of histone acetyltransferases (Wu et al., 2015), together with the release of histone deacetylases (HDACs) from target loci through degradation of Aux/IAA repressors (Long et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research on auxin signaling mechanisms.

claim: Chromatin state change is one mechanism that allows the temporal integration of signals in eukaryotes, including plants.
source: Chromatin state change is one mechanism that allows the temporal integration of signals in eukaryotes, including plants (Angel et al., 2011; Coda et al., 2017; Nahmad and Lander, 2011; Sun et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous research on chromatin-based signal integration.

claim: Time integration of the auxin signal in cells leaving the CZ is plausibly set by progressive acetylation of histones triggered by ARFs at their target loci.
source: It is thus plausible that time integration of the auxin signal in cells leaving the CZ is set by progressive acetylation of histones triggered by ARFs at their target loci.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on known mechanisms of chromatin regulation and the experimental results.

claim: Chromatin deacetylation represses auxin signaling in the CZ.
source: As chromatin deacetylation also represses auxin signaling in the CZ (Ma et al., 2019), balancing the acetylation status of ARF target loci could provide a mechanism to tightly link stem cell maintenance to differentiation by precisely positioning organ initiation at the boundary of the stem cell niche, while at the same time allowing sequential organ initiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The existence of high definition spatio-temporal auxin gradients suggests that the robustness of SAM patterning results from highly reproducible spatio-temporal positional information.
source: The existence of high definition spatio-temporal auxin gradients suggests that as for several morphogens in animals (Nahmad and Lander, 2011; Dessaud et al., 2007; Scherz et al., 2007; Maden, 2002) the robustness of SAM patterning results from highly reproducible spatio-temporal positional information.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed precision of auxin distribution and is compared to animal morphogen systems.

claim: Auxin maxima could first emerge from the CZ at the confluence of centripetal auxin fluxes.
source: Our results indicate that auxin maxima could first emerge from the CZ at the confluence of centripetal auxin fluxes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the PIN1 polarity patterns and auxin distribution dynamics.

claim: Confluences creating auxin maxima would at the same time divert fluxes away from areas where auxin minima appear.
source: Confluences creating auxin maxima would at the same time divert fluxes away from areas where auxin minima appear (Figure 3M).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the analysis of PIN1 polarity organization and auxin distribution.

claim: Early developing flowers act as auxin production centers.
source: Further analysis of the spatio-temporal control of auxin distribution needs also to consider that early developing flowers act as auxin production centers.
evidence: The claim is supported by YUC expression patterns in developing flowers.

claim: Early developing flowers could provide a memory of the developmental pattern through lateral inhibition and contribute positively to a self-sustained auxin distribution pattern by providing auxin to the system.
source: These flowers could not only provide a memory of the developmental pattern through lateral inhibition but also contribute positively to a self-sustained auxin distribution pattern by providing auxin to the system (Figure 3M).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observed YUC expression and PIN1 polarity patterns.

claim: The stem cell niche could act as a system-wide organizer of auxin transport.
source: Finally, our work indicates that the stem cell niche could act as a system-wide organizer of auxin transport, consistent with previous work (de Reuille et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the PIN1 polarity patterns showing convergence toward the center and is consistent with previous modeling work.

claim: The stem cell niche acting as an organizer of auxin transport could provide another layer of regulation tightly coordinating differentiation with the presence of a largely auxin-insensitive stem cell niche.
source: This could provide another layer of regulation tightly coordinating differentiation with the presence of a largely auxin-insensitive stem cell niche (Vernoux et al., 2011; Ma et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the inferred role of the stem cell niche and previous research on auxin insensitivity in the CZ.
